name: wopee-mcp

tools.name: wopee_create_blank_suite
tools.description: Create a new empty analysis suite in the current project. Use this as the first step when you want to manually build a test suite — the returned suite UUID is needed by wopee_generate_artifact, wopee_fetch_artifact, wopee_update_artifact, and wopee_dispatch_agent. If you want to auto-analyze a web app instead, use wopee_dispatch_analysis which creates and populates a suite in one step. Takes no input parameters; uses WOPEE_PROJECT_UUID from environment. Not idempotent: each call creates a new suite. Returns the suite object with UUID, name, type, and status. Fails if WOPEE_PROJECT_UUID is not configured.

tools.name: wopee_fetch_analysis_suites
tools.description: List all analysis suites in the current project. Returns an array of suite objects with UUIDs, names, types (ANALYSIS, AGENT, etc.), and running statuses (IDLE, IN_PROGRESS, FINISHED). Use this to discover existing suites before calling other tools — you need a suite UUID for wopee_generate_artifact, wopee_fetch_artifact, wopee_update_artifact, and wopee_dispatch_agent. Read-only: does not create or modify anything. Takes no input; works in the connected project. Returns an empty array if no suites exist.

tools.name: wopee_fetch_executed_test_cases
tools.description: Retrieve results of test cases executed by the autonomous agent. Returns each test case with its execution status (IN_PROGRESS, FINISHED, FAILED), agent report (natural language findings), and code report (technical details). Read-only: does not trigger any execution. Use this after wopee_dispatch_agent to check results — if status is IN_PROGRESS, wait and call again. Requires suite UUID. Optionally accepts an analysis identifier (e.g. A068, found in suite data) to filter to a specific analysis run. Returns an empty array if no test cases have been executed in this suite. Do NOT use this to fetch test artifacts like user stories or code — use wopee_fetch_artifact for that.

suiteUuid.description: UUID of the analysis suite to fetch executed test cases for

analysisIdentifier.description: Analysis identifier of the suite (ex. A068). Can be found in the analysis suite data.

tools.name: wopee_fetch_recent_executions
tools.description: Fetch the most recent test case executions for the current project (up to 20, newest first). Use this to check the status of recently dispatched tests without needing to remember specific suite UUIDs. Returns each run's verdict (PASSED, FAILED, or INCOMPLETE — the run never established a result, e.g. an infrastructure error, and says nothing about the application) or, for a run with no verdict yet, its execution status (IN_QUEUE, IN_PROGRESS, FINISHED, FAILED, STOPPED), plus agent reports. Takes no input; uses WOPEE_PROJECT_UUID from environment. Prefer this tool when the user asks 'what's the status?' or 'how did the tests go?' and you don't have the specific suite UUID handy.

tools.name: wopee_fetch_test_inventory
tools.description: The authoritative tool for how many tests exist and their latest status. Returns, per analysis, the FULL list of authored test cases joined with their latest execution status — including never-run ones as NOT_RUN. Use this for questions like 'how many tests do I have', 'list the scenarios/test cases in A001', or 'show executed and not-run tests in one table'. Terminology: a 'scenario' is a test case; test cases are grouped under user stories (US001) and identified as US001:TC001. Reusable blocks (user story R001) are counted separately (reusableBlockCount) and are building blocks, not runnable, so they never carry an execution status. Regular tests are all non-R001 test cases. Read-only. Takes an optional analysisIdentifier (e.g. A001) to scope to one analysis; omit to cover every analysis in the project. Prefer this over wopee_fetch_recent_executions / wopee_fetch_executed_test_cases when the user asks about totals or the complete list — those return only test cases that have already run. Each test case carries executedTestCaseUuid (the latest run's uuid, the same one wopee_dispatch_agent returns) and verdictGateDisagreed (true when a verdict gate disagreed with a PASSED verdict — report it alongside the pass). Status UNKNOWN means the execution history could not be read (the reason is in the analysis's executionHistoryError); do not report such tests as not run.

analysisIdentifier.description: Optional analysis identifier (e.g. A001) to scope the inventory to a single analysis. Omit to include every analysis in the project.

tools.name: wopee_fetch_variables
tools.description: Read the run-time variables (additionalVariables) that drive analysis/agent runs, at either level. level: PROJECT returns the project-level variables (the connected project); level: ANALYSIS returns a specific analysis suite's variables and requires suiteUuid, including the analysis' own TESTING_USERNAME, TESTING_PASSWORD, WOPEE_DEVICE and WOPEE_BROWSER when its settings set them; each overrides the project variable of the same key for that analysis. Read-only. Returns a JSON string array of { key, value, sourceType } entries, or [] when none are set; secret values (e.g. passwords) read as "***". Use wopee_fetch_analysis_suites to discover suite UUIDs.

level.description: Which variable set to read. PROJECT reads the project-level variables (the connected project). ANALYSIS reads a specific analysis suite's variables and requires suiteUuid.

suiteUuid.description: UUID of the analysis suite to read variables from. Required when level is ANALYSIS; ignored when level is PROJECT.

tools.name: wopee_update_variables
tools.description: Upsert the run-time variables (additionalVariables) that drive analysis/agent runs, at either level. level: PROJECT writes the project-level variables (the connected project); level: ANALYSIS writes a specific analysis suite's variables and requires suiteUuid. Merge semantics: keys in variables[] are added or overwritten, existing keys not listed are preserved. Keys must be uppercase (e.g. BASE_URL); the server re-sanitizes and drops invalid keys. Returns a confirmation on success.

level.description: Which variable set to write. PROJECT writes the project-level variables (the connected project). ANALYSIS writes a specific analysis suite's variables and requires suiteUuid.

suiteUuid.description: UUID of the analysis suite to write variables to. Required when level is ANALYSIS; ignored when level is PROJECT.

key.description: Variable name. Must be uppercase with underscores only (e.g. MY_VAR, BASE_URL).

value.description: Variable value. Must be a non-empty string.

variables.description: Variables to upsert. Each needs an uppercase key (e.g. BASE_URL) and a non-empty value. Merge semantics: keys listed here are added or overwritten; existing keys not listed here are preserved.

tools.name: wopee_setup_check
tools.description: Verify that Wopee.io is connected: returns the project name and UUID, app URL, plan, steps left, reset time and the Commander link for the project of WOPEE_API_KEY, and names the problem when the key belongs to another project than WOPEE_PROJECT_UUID, the UUID is missing or the key is rejected. Read-only, takes no input. Call it as the last step of a setup and whenever a tool answers Not Authorised!.

tools.name: wopee_dispatch_analysis
tools.description: Create a new analysis suite AND dispatch an AI crawling agent in one step. The agent opens a real browser, navigates from the starting URL, discovers pages, and maps the application structure. Use this when you want to auto-analyze a web app — it combines suite creation and crawling. Use wopee_create_blank_suite instead if you want to manually populate the suite. The crawl starts from the starting URL set in the project settings in Commander; this tool has no starting URL, login or cookie inputs. Optional inputs: free-text instructions to guide the crawl, custom variables (e.g. login details the instructions refer to), and a rerun of an existing suite. Not idempotent: each call creates a new suite and starts a new crawl. Side effects: creates a suite and execution records on the platform. Rate limit: 10 seconds between dispatches per project; concurrent calls auto-retry with exponential backoff. Returns the suite UUID, analysis identifier and status; poll wopee_fetch_analysis_suites every 30-60 s to follow it (5-10 minutes).

additionalVariables.description: Additional environment variables for the analysis. Each variable needs a key (uppercase, e.g. BASE_URL) and a non-empty value.

key.description: Variable name. Must be uppercase with underscores only (e.g. MY_VAR, BASE_URL).

value.description: Variable value. Must be a non-empty string.

rerun.description: If provided, reruns an existing analysis suite instead of creating a new one. Requires suiteUuid, analysisIdentifier, and mode.

suiteUuid.description: UUID of the existing suite to rerun.

analysisIdentifier.description: Analysis identifier of the existing suite to rerun.

mode.description: Rerun mode: FULL reruns the entire analysis (crawling + analysis), CRAWLING reruns only the crawling phase.

tools.name: wopee_dispatch_agent
tools.description: Dispatch an autonomous AI agent to execute specific test cases. The agent opens a real browser, navigates the app, follows the test case's steps, and reports results. A test case without steps runs as it is: the agent follows its description and the run records the steps it took, so never generate steps first just to be able to run it. Tests run ASYNCHRONOUSLY (1-3 minutes). This tool returns tracking info confirming dispatch — NOT final results. Do NOT interpret the response as pass/fail. Poll wopee_fetch_recent_executions or wopee_fetch_executed_test_cases every 30-60 s for the verdict (inside the Commander Assistant, results also arrive as a chat notification). Prerequisite: test cases must exist in the suite (generate with wopee_generate_artifact type USER_STORIES_WITH_TEST_CASES).

suiteUuid.description: UUID of the suite to dispatch the agent for

analysisIdentifier.description: Analysis identifier of the suite to dispatch the agent for

testCaseId.description: ID of the test case belonging to the user story to dispatch the agent for (ex. TC001)

userStoryId.description: ID of the user story that the test case belongs to (ex. US001)

testCases.description: Chosen test cases to dispatch the agent for

tools.name: wopee_fetch_artifact
tools.description: Retrieve a specific test artifact from a suite. Returns the artifact content as text. Use this to review what wopee_generate_artifact created, or to retrieve existing artifacts before editing with wopee_update_artifact. Does NOT modify any data — this is a read-only operation. If the requested artifact type has not been generated yet for this suite, returns an empty result. For PLAYWRIGHT_CODE, you must provide the test case identifier (e.g. 'US004:TC006'); omitting it returns an error. For all other types, the identifier parameter is ignored.

type.description: Type of test artifact to retrieve. One of: APP_CONTEXT (application description), GENERAL_USER_STORIES (stories without test cases), USER_STORIES (stories with test cases), PLAYWRIGHT_CODE (generated test code — requires identifier), PROJECT_CONTEXT (project-level context).

suiteUuid.description: UUID of the analysis suite to fetch artifacts from. Get this from wopee_fetch_analysis_suites.

identifier.description: Test case identifier in format 'US004:TC006'. Required only when type is PLAYWRIGHT_CODE. Ignored for all other artifact types.

tools.name: wopee_update_artifact
tools.description: Create or overwrite a test artifact in a suite with caller-supplied content. The full content is replaced, not patched. Use this to upload your own APP_CONTEXT (e.g. built from JIRA / Confluence), user stories, project context, or Playwright code, or to fix / refine an artifact previously authored by wopee_generate_artifact. Works on any suite, including freshly-created blank suites with no prior generation — the artifact does not need to exist beforehand. Use wopee_generate_artifact instead when you want the Wopee.io AI engine to author the content from scratch. On success, returns confirmation. On failure (e.g. invalid suite UUID, storage misconfiguration), returns an error message. Idempotent: calling with the same content multiple times produces the same result.

type.description: Type of test artifact to update. One of: APP_CONTEXT, GENERAL_USER_STORIES, USER_STORIES, PLAYWRIGHT_CODE (requires identifier), PROJECT_CONTEXT. Must match the type used when the artifact was generated.

content.description: The complete new content to replace the existing artifact. This is a destructive overwrite — the entire previous content is replaced. Pass the full updated content, not a partial diff.

suiteUuid.description: UUID of the analysis suite containing the artifact to update. Get this from wopee_fetch_analysis_suites.

identifier.description: Test case identifier in format 'US004:TC006'. Required only when type is PLAYWRIGHT_CODE. Ignored for all other artifact types.

tools.name: wopee_generate_artifact
tools.description: Generate AI-powered test artifacts for a suite using the Wopee.io AI engine. Each call creates one artifact type — call multiple times for different types. Generation order matters: APP_CONTEXT must be generated before user stories, and user stories before test cases. If called out of order, the AI may produce lower quality results. By default the call waits up to 5 minutes for the generation and returns the generated artifact: APP_CONTEXT or GENERAL_USER_STORIES, or the suite's USER_STORIES (stories with their test cases and steps) for every other type. No wopee_fetch_artifact call is needed after it. With async: true, for TEST_CASES and USER_STORIES_WITH_TEST_CASES only, the call returns "Queued: …" at once; read the result later with wopee_fetch_artifact. If the 5 minutes pass first, the call fails with a [TIMEOUT] error while the generation goes on: do not call again (that starts a second generation), read the result later with wopee_fetch_artifact, and pass async: true next time for a long TEST_CASES or USER_STORIES_WITH_TEST_CASES generation. Do NOT use this to hand-edit existing artifacts — use wopee_update_artifact instead. TEST_CASES runs in UPDATE mode by default: existing test cases keep their steps and run history, and `instructions` says what to add or change. Destructive generations are mode CREATE (replaces the test cases in scope and deletes their steps, runs and code), USER_STORIES_WITH_TEST_CASES (rebuilds every story and test case) and TEST_CASE_STEPS (replaces the steps of the test cases in scope): use them only when the user explicitly asks for that, and scope them with selectedUserStories / selectedTestCases when the user named stories or test cases. Login credentials are project variables, referenced in steps as ${TESTING_USERNAME} / ${TESTING_PASSWORD}: check which exist with wopee_fetch_variables and set missing ones with wopee_update_variables before generating. Never put a password or other secret value in `instructions` — it would be copied into the artifact.

type.description: Type of test artifact to generate. One of: APP_CONTEXT, GENERAL_USER_STORIES, USER_STORIES_WITH_TEST_CASES, TEST_CASES, TEST_CASE_STEPS, REUSABLE_TEST_CASES, REUSABLE_TEST_CASE_STEPS. Start with APP_CONTEXT, then generate stories and test cases from it.

suiteUuid.description: UUID of the analysis suite to generate artifacts for. Get this from wopee_create_blank_suite or wopee_fetch_analysis_suites.

mode.description: TEST_CASES only. UPDATE (default) keeps every existing test case with its steps and run history, and adds or changes test cases around them. CREATE replaces the test cases of the stories in scope — of the whole suite when selectedUserStories is empty — and deletes their steps, run history and Playwright code. Use CREATE only when the user explicitly asks to start over.

selectedUserStories.description: User story ids to limit the generation to, e.g. ['US001', 'US003']. Leave empty for every story in the suite. Used by TEST_CASES and TEST_CASE_STEPS.

selectedTestCases.description: Test case identifiers to limit TEST_CASE_STEPS to, e.g. ['US001:TC002']. Leave empty for every test case in scope. Regenerating steps replaces the steps those test cases have.

instructions.description: What the user asked for, in their words, e.g. 'add a negative test for an expired card'. Passed to the AI engine as the change request; without it, UPDATE removes no test case.

async.description: TEST_CASES and USER_STORIES_WITH_TEST_CASES only. true returns as soon as the generation is queued instead of waiting for it (a large suite can take several minutes); the content is then read later with wopee_fetch_artifact. Default false: wait and return the generated artifact.

tools.name: wopee_create_github_issue
tools.description: Create a new GitHub issue in the project's connected repository. Use this to report bugs found during testing, track test failures, or create action items from chat discussions. For a failed test, pass its executedTestCaseUuid so the issue carries the run's evidence (failing step, expected vs actual, screenshot, report link). The issue is created by the Wopee.io GitHub App and names the requester in its body. Requires a GitHub repository linked to the project and WOPEE_PROJECT_UUID to be set.

title.description: The title of the GitHub issue

body.description: The body/description of the GitHub issue (supports Markdown). Kept verbatim, above anything Wopee.io adds from the test run.

labels.description: Optional labels to apply to the issue (e.g., ['bug', 'testing'])

executedTestCaseUuid.description: UUID of the executed test case the issue is about (the executedTestCaseUuid shown by wopee_fetch_recent_executions and wopee_dispatch_agent, or uuid in wopee_fetch_executed_test_cases). When set, Wopee.io adds the failing step, expected vs actual, the failing step's screenshot and a link to the run in Commander, so the body only needs your own analysis.

tools.name: wopee_search_docs
tools.description: Search the Wopee.io documentation (docs.wopee.io, from its llms-full.txt) and return the best matching sections with their page URL. Use it for questions about setup, configuration, environment variables, integrations (Playwright, Cypress, WebdriverIO, Robot Framework), MCP clients, CI, concepts and troubleshooting, before guessing. Read-only, needs no API key, and does not touch the project. Results are cached for an hour.

query.description: What to look up in the Wopee.io documentation, in plain words or exact names (e.g. 'WOPEE_PROJECT_UUID', 'cypress install plugin', 'self-healing locators').

maxResults.description: Number of sections to return, 1 to 10. Default 5.
